[file][omnibox][ntp] Ensure files have no background

* Attachments can have 2 backgrounds - one for the icon, and one
for the box around the icon.
* Files should have no background for the icon and the box, while
PDFs should have a background for the box
* Currently, all files have a background, and the icon for the file
has a background
* However, NTP requires a background for the box.
* Fix: Remove the icon and box background by default unless
overridden by the surface, such as NTP.
* Ensure PDF type is detected, and overrides the default settings
so PDFs always have a background box.

Fix CHECK failure in FilenameElider::GetLineLengths

In `FilenameElider::GetLineLengths()`, `render_text_->GetDisplayText()`
with `ELIDE_HEAD` was compared against `render_text_->text()` to check
whether the text fits on a single line without elision.
However, when `RenderText` does not elide text in single-line mode,
`GetDisplayText()` returns the layout text rather than the original
`text()`. Because `RenderText::EnsureLayoutTextUpdated()` replaces
certain characters in `layout_text_` (such as tabs, newlines, control
characters, Private Use Area code points, and noncharacters),
`GetDisplayText()` differs from `text()` whenever the input contains
any of these characters. When such a string fits on a single line,
`tentative_second_line == render_text_->text()` evaluates to false even
though no elision occurred, causing execution to fall through and hit
the CHECK.

Fix this by comparing the `ELIDE_HEAD` display text against the
unelided display text (`NO_ELIDE`) instead of `render_text_->text()`.

arc: Keep destination file descriptor open until posted write runs

ShareInfoFileStreamAdapter::WriteToFile() previously posted a blocking
write to its worker sequence using the raw integer value of dest_fd_. If
references to the adapter were dropped while the write was queued (such
as during early session teardown), the adapter was destroyed on the IO
thread and ScopedFD closed the descriptor before the worker task ran,
causing the write operation to target a closed or reassigned descriptor.

Holding a scoped_refptr to |this| in the background write task would
keep dest_fd_ open, but could cause cross-thread object resurrection
(calling AddRef on an object whose refcount reached 0 on the UI thread),
leading to a DCHECK(!in_dtor_) crash or UAF.

To decouple the destination file descriptor lifetime from the adapter's
refcount, wrap dest_fd_ in a scoped_refptr<base::RefCountedData<base::ScopedFD>>.
The background write task binds only dest_fd_ and the buffer, ensuring
the file descriptor remains open until the write finishes without
resurrecting or extending the lifetime of ShareInfoFileStreamAdapter.

Bug: b:501380633
Test: unit_tests --gtest_filter="ShareInfoFileStreamAdapterTest.*"

Map Reading Mode selections to translated PDF blocks

Adds TranslatedSelectionMapper.getAxSelection, which maps a selection in
the translated Reading Mode panel to the AX selection of all of the text
in the blocks that contain it, i.e. the selection that would be made by
selecting those blocks in the untranslated panel.

The selected blocks are found from the first and last text nodes in a
block that have selected text other than whitespace, so selections that
only touch the edge of a block, only select whitespace between blocks,
or only select text outside of blocks are ignored.

The mapper is not used yet.

[Keyboard Shortcuts] Add close shortcuts to TaskManagerActivity

On Android, TaskManagerActivity is a standalone
ChromeBaseAppCompatActivity without WindowAndroid or AcceleratorManager,
so window-close shortcuts do not dismiss it as they do on Desktop's
TaskManagerView. Override Activity.onKeyDown behind
ChromeFeatureList.UNIVERSAL_KEYBOARD_HANDLING to finish the Activity on
non-repeat Ctrl+W, Ctrl+Shift+W, Alt+F4, and unmodified Escape, running
after focused child views (such as the search input) get first chance to
handle Escape.

Use fake fullscreen on Mac in flaky fullscreen tests

These tests check browser UI while the window is fullscreen, but on Mac
they go through a real AppKit fullscreen transition. That transition is
slow and can fail when another window has focus, which happens a lot
when browser_tests run in parallel. When it fails, the window stays
windowed and FullscreenWaiter waits until the test times out.

None of these tests are about the transition itself, so use
ScopedFakeNSWindowFullscreen on Mac like other fullscreen browser tests
already do.

Entering and exiting fullscreen then finishes right away.

[iOS][TTC] Stop session asynchronously on backend closure or fatal error

When TtcConversation notifies TtcSessionController of backend closure (OnConversationClosed()) or a fatal error (OnConversationError()), calling StopSession() synchronously tears down TtcConversation and TtcBackend while the backend callback is still on the stack.

Match Desktop SessionControllerImpl::EndSessionAsync() by transitioning lifecycle_ to kFinished immediately and posting StopSession() to the current sequenced task runner via StopSessionAsync(). Also stop any existing _AIPrototypingCoordinator before creating a new instance in -[SceneCoordinator openAIMenu].

[HiC] Fix CanvasTransform with CSS object-fit

When CSS object-fit is used the canvas bitmap may not fill the canvas
element's layout box or may be clipped or may be rescaled. Previously,
this was not accounted for in the CanvasTransform resulting in
incorrectly positioned elements for hit testing and selection.

Fix the issue by keeping the offset for the bitmap in the canvas child
paint state and then applying it to the canvas transform.

[browser_actuator] Test internals recording on the FCM wake-up path

The FCM integration tests in
`browser_actuator_message_handler_unittest.cc` only check that the
session recorder exists. They don't catch the recorder missing the
wake-up or recording its reply first.

This CL checks the recorded events for the FCM `StartSession` and
Glic experimental triggering wake-ups. Each downstream payload is
recorded before the upstream reply it triggered: `StartSession`
before `StartSessionAck`, then the bundled Glic payload before its
reply. Test-only change.

83a6af7f37b59a4a348d25acb53854b7c748661f [ diff ] 
[browser_actuator] Record internals sessions from first FCM message

chrome://browser-actuator-internals records sessions through
`SessionStreamRecorderFactory`, which is registered as a
`TransportHandlerFactory`. A session's recorder is only created when
its first payload is dispatched, after handlers that registered
earlier. For an FCM `StartSession`, `ControlTransportHandler` sends
`StartSessionAck` before the recorder sees the wake-up, so the page
shows the reply first. A downstream `CloseSession` or `CloseChannel`
that tears down the session during dispatch is never recorded. The
recorder also rebuilds each payload into a new envelope, which drops
`sequence_number`.

This CL makes `SessionStreamRecorderFactory` a
`TransportSessionRegistry::Observer` instead of a handler factory.
It creates a recorder when the session is created and records
downstream messages through `OnDownstreamMessage()` from the parent
CL, before any handler runs and before the upstream replies they
trigger. Closed session history is capped at 100 sessions. Recording
still only runs when `BrowserActuatorInternals` is on.

Reading guide:
Tier 1 (Core architecture):
- `session_stream_recorder.{h,cc}`: recorder lifetime follows
  `OnSessionRegistered()` / `OnSessionRemoved()`
Tier 2 (Behavioral tests):
- `session_stream_recorder_unittest.cc`: arrival order, ID reuse,
  and the retained session cap
- `transport_service_integration_unittest.cc`: `StartSession` is
  recorded before `StartSessionAck`; downstream `CloseSession` /
  `CloseChannel` and the upstream `CloseSession` from
  `TransportSession::Close()` are recorded
- `browser_actuator_internals_ui_mojo_impl_unittest.cc`: same order
  through the internals Mojo handler
Tier 3 (Pre-verified plumbing):
- `transport_service_impl.*`, `common.h` LINT target, internals
  `README.md`

Stack:
1. https://crrev.com/c/8665080 - Downstream observer hook
2. https://crrev.com/c/8665499 - Record sessions from first FCM
   message (this CL)
3. https://crrev.com/c/8665758 - FCM wake-up recording tests

[PageLoadMetrics] Fix flake in InputEventsForFormSubmission

In PageLoadMetricsBrowserTest.InputEventsForFormSubmission, the key
input form submission subtest records
Navigation.Timeline.InteractionToActualNavigationStart.Duration via
base::UmaHistogramTimes(timeline.start - timeline.user_interaction),
which truncates sub-millisecond durations to 0 ms. On fast bots, the
IPC from SimulateKeyPress to form submission completes in under 1 ms,
causing GetTotalSum() > 0 (and InteractionToNavigationFinished >
total_duration) to fail when the sample lands in the 0 bucket. Relax
those assertions to EXPECT_GE since ExpectTotalCount(..., 1) already
verifies that a sample was recorded.

Also disable omnibox::internal::kWebUIOmniboxPopup and
omnibox::internal::kWebUIOmniboxAimPopup in PageLoadMetricsBrowserTest

45ce8a1928013519197967b3089b935b8d9408c2
parent
b1f48233631454435189cc99297f576a5e61a152 [ diff ] 
Reject renderer-disallowed transition qualifiers in BeginNavigation

VerifyBeginNavigationCommonParams() checks that the navigation's
PageTransition is web-triggerable via PageTransitionIsWebTriggerable().
However, PageTransitionIsWebTriggerable() strips qualifiers via
PageTransitionStripQualifier() and only validates the core transition
type.

Additionally, RenderFrameHostImpl::ValidateDidCommitParams() only
rejects renderer-disallowed qualifiers at commit time if they were not
already present on NavigationRequest::common_params().transition. As a
result, a compromised renderer could supply browser-only qualifiers
(such as PAGE_TRANSITION_FROM_API or PAGE_TRANSITION_FROM_ADDRESS_BAR)
in BeginNavigation alongside a web-triggerable core type (such as
PAGE_TRANSITION_LINK), bypassing both checks.

Explicitly reject transitions carrying any qualifier in
PAGE_TRANSITION_RENDERER_DISALLOWED_QUALIFIERS_MASK in
VerifyBeginNavigationCommonParams() with a dedicated
RFHI_BEGIN_NAVIGATION_DISALLOWED_QUALIFIER bad message reason.

parent
117002aa42583fdfae6f44b872d26e8281d4fc5c [ diff ] 
[browser_actuator] Report downstream messages to transport observers

`TransportMessageObserver` only reports upstream messages. A
diagnostic consumer such as `SessionStreamRecorderFactory` can only
see downstream messages by registering as a
`TransportHandlerFactory`, which ties it to lazy handler creation
and to handler dispatch order.

This CL adds `TransportMessageObserver::OnDownstreamMessage()`.
`TransportChannelImpl` passes a `DownstreamMessageCallback` through
`TransportSessionRegistryImpl` to each `TransportSessionImpl`, which
runs it right before dispatching to handlers. The stream path
reports once per envelope, and the FCM wake-up path reports once per
payload. If the callback destroys the session, dispatch stops.
`SessionStreamRecorderFactory` gets an empty override until the next
CL. No behavior change.

Stack:
1. https://crrev.com/c/8665080 - Downstream observer hook (this CL)
2. https://crrev.com/c/8665499 - Record sessions from first FCM
   message
3. https://crrev.com/c/8665758 - FCM wake-up recording tests

Fix CanCreateSession() callback handling in ModelSubscriber

- Emplace empty capabilities_ in ModelSubscriber::OnDisconnect() so
  pending CanCreateSession() callbacks still flush when disconnecting
  before CapabilitiesUpdated() arrives.
- Return ready closures from FlushModelClientCallbacks(),
  FlushCanCreateSessionCallbacks(), and FlushAllCallbacks() and run
  them via RunAll() after subscriber state updates finish so callbacks
  can safely destroy the subscriber re-entrantly.

[WebUI Omnibox] Exit keyword mode on focus location command when focused

With the full WebUI omnibox popup, running the focus location command
(`IDC_FOCUS_LOCATION`, e.g. File > Open Location on Mac) while the popup
is focused in keyword mode didn't exit keyword mode, unlike pressing
Cmd/Ctrl+L in the popup. The command doesn't go through the popup's
keydown handler; it reaches the popup as SetFocus(showFullUrl=true).

In `onSetFocus_()`, exit keyword mode for such focus-location requests
if the input already has DOM focus, matching the shortcut handling and
`OmniboxViewViews::SetFocus()`. Keyword mode is kept when focus returns
to a blurred draft.

5b3a5b356cfbc3bb9ab0b28c7fcc8631dd66df31 [ diff ] 
[Cast Remoting] Notify sources when remoting is re-enabled mid-session

Currently, a page refresh is required in order to enable media remoting
mid-cast session.

The root cause is that if a user disables media remoting while there is
not an active remoting session, the CastRemotingConnector clears the
sink_metadata_ even though the MediaRemoter is not stopped. The remoter
thus does not call OnSinkAvailable() again. The OnPrefChanged() method
also does not properly notify registered remoting bridges when the
preference is re-enabled.

The fix here is to keep when USER_DISABLED occurs without an active
bridge, gate OnSinkAvailable() notifications on remoting_allowed_, and
notify registered bridges of sink availability when remoting is
re-enabled in OnPrefChanged().

ash: Alt+Tab past a window whose transient child is active

Problem: When a transient child of the most recently used window, such
as a bubble or popup, holds activation, the first Alt+Tab reselects that
window. The focused Full WebUI omnibox hits this because its frameless
popup widget [1] is a transient child of the browser window [2] and
holds activation while focused [3]. CreateWindowList() collapses the
cycle list to transient roots [4], while WindowCycleList::Step() resets
to the first entry when active_window_before_window_cycle_ does not
match it [5].

Solution: Resolve active_window_before_window_cycle_ to the active
window's transient root, guarded by a new default-enabled
kWindowCycleUseTransientRoot killswitch. This also applies to other
active transient children, such as bookmark and permission bubbles.
WindowCycleList::Step() only resets to the first entry on kForward, for
cases like overview or minimized windows where no listed window is
active [5], so Alt+Shift+Tab from a bubble already switches windows on
the first press. The omnibox popup also cannot avoid activation locally
because its WebContents needs activation for key input [3].

[1]
https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/966e873a6671e89d61e1e3633fd247b97e4b20a3:chrome/browser/ui/views/omnibox/omnibox_popup_presenter_base.cc;l=523-528
[2]
https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/966e873a6671e89d61e1e3633fd247b97e4b20a3:ui/views/widget/native_widget_aura.cc;l=299-306
[3]
https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/966e873a6671e89d61e1e3633fd247b97e4b20a3:chrome/browser/ui/views/omnibox/omnibox_popup_full_presenter.cc;l=238-240
[4]
https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/966e873a6671e89d61e1e3633fd247b97e4b20a3:ash/wm/window_cycle/window_cycle_controller.cc;l=390-399
[5]
https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/966e873a6671e89d61e1e3633fd247b97e4b20a3:ash/wm/window_cycle/window_cycle_list.cc;l=186-200

[DTC][CSS] Record Android storage encryption status in UMA

Add the Enterprise.DeviceSignals.StorageEncryption.Status histogram,
recorded each time the disk_encryption signal is collected on Android.

The server only receives the mapped ENABLED/DISABLED/UNKNOWN value, so
this shows how the mapping behaves in the field: how often full-disk
encryption statuses (ACTIVE, ACTIVE_DEFAULT_KEY, ACTIVATING) are still
reported, how often the status is UNSUPPORTED, and whether a newer
Android version reports a status Chrome doesn't recognize.

- Buckets 0-5 are the DevicePolicyManager.ENCRYPTION_STATUS_* values;
  any other value is recorded as 6 (Unrecognized). The Java @IntDef is
  kept in sync with enums.xml via LINT.IfChange.
- Nothing is recorded when DevicePolicyManager is unavailable.

[Extensions] Restrict mimeHandlerPrivate to allowlisted extensions

The mimeHandlerPrivate API only depended on the mime_types_handler
manifest key. That key used to be limited to the extensions in
kMIMETypeHandlersAllowlist. After the public mimeHandler API launched,
any extension can declare mime_types_handler, so mimeHandlerPrivate
became available to any extension that declares the key.

After this change, mimeHandlerPrivate is only available to the
extensions in kMIMETypeHandlersAllowlist (the PDF viewer, QuickOffice
and the browser_tests test extension), on every channel. Other
extensions that declare mime_types_handler still get the public
mimeHandler API.

[Input] Reset gesture scroll state in SetupInputRouter

When a RenderWidget is destroyed mid-scroll or mid-fling (for example,
due to a renderer crash or cross-document navigation) and later
recreated on the same RenderWidgetHostImpl, SetupInputRouter() replaces
input_router_ without stopping any active fling or clearing the scroll
tracking flags on RenderInputRouter. A subsequent GestureScrollBegin on
the recreated widget then fails DCHECK(!is_in_gesture_scroll_).

Stop any active fling on the existing InputRouter and reset
is_currently_scrolling_viewport_, scroll_peak_gpu_mem_tracker_,
is_in_gesture_scroll_, is_in_touchpad_gesture_fling_, and
gsb_filtered_for_paint_holding_ in SetupInputRouter().

glic: Ignore native platform events in drag-and-drop browsertests

In browser_tests on Windows, multiple test processes run concurrently on
the shared desktop. While asynchronous drag-and-drop operations (such as
in GlicDragAndDropTestBase) wait for Blink's StartDragging IPC, native
Win32 mouse events (e.g. WM_MOUSEMOVE from other test processes opening
or resizing windows) can clobber aura::Env's last_mouse_location_. This
causes WebContentsViewAura::StartDragging() to fail its bounds check and
abort the drag before DragDropClient::StartDragAndDrop() is invoked,
leading to flaky timeouts in tests such as
GlicDragAndDropPolicyTest.testWebToGlicDragDlpBlocked.

This CL sets ui::PlatformEventSource::SetIgnoreNativePlatformEvents(true)
during SetUpOnMainThread() in GlicDragAndDropTestBase and restores the
previous value in TearDownOnMainThread(), protecting synthetic drags from
interfering native platform events.

Remove distillation state and status from ReadAnythingController

ReadAnythingController owns Reading Mode's presentation lifecycle, not
content distillation, yet it had two similar-sounding distillation
methods: OnDistillationStatus() and OnDistillationStateChanged().

OnDistillationStatus() only logs the omnibox entry point's distillation
metrics. Move it, along with last_open_trigger_, into
ReadAnythingUntrustedPageHandler, which already has the distillation
status.

Rename ReadAnythingController::OnDistillationStateChanged() to
OnEmptyStateChanged(). Taking DistillationState in
OnDistillationStateChanged() set a precedent for adding distillation
logic to the controller - the new method clarifies its purpose.

[glic] Skip hidden TabUnderlineView updates on tab switches

Every browser tab hosts a TabUnderlineView that subscribes to active tab
changes and theme updates. Whenever a user switches tabs, every tab's
TabUnderlineView runs OnActiveTabChanged().

Previously, OnActiveTabChanged() and OnThemeChanged() unconditionally
queried the widget's ColorProvider via GetEffectColors(), allocated a
new color vector, and called SchedulePaint() even when the underline
view wasn't showing. Because SchedulePaint() only checks visibility at
the very end, every tab switch paid an O(M) color lookup and allocation
cost across all M tabs in the window (~5.2 us per tab, or 0.13-0.50 ms
for 25-100 tabs) even when Glic was never opened or its underline was
hidden.

This CL short-circuits OnActiveTabChanged() and OnThemeChanged() when
!IsShowing(), and refreshes colors_ in Show() right before the underline
becomes visible. A browser test verifies that hidden underlines skip
color updates on tab activation and initialize colors when shown.

Benchmark & analysis: http://artifacts/APOWonRJih

parent
0d79cba0c6e084ee95ca9b81761aaa116dcd648b [ diff ] 
[dbsc] Run key restore callback when the session is gone

OnSessionKeyRestored() returned without running its callback when the
session was deleted while its binding key was being unwrapped. For a
federated registration this dropped CheckFederatedProviderKey(), so the
registration never reported a result.

Run the callback with std::nullopt instead, like the other failure
paths. The federated registration now fails with
kInvalidFederatedSessionProviderFailedToRestoreKey. Since a key is now
only passed when the session exists, the provider-session-missing
branch in CheckFederatedProviderKey() was unreachable and is now a
CHECK.

For refreshes, RefreshSessionInternal() now runs and returns early on
the null key. Waiting requests were already unblocked when the session
was deleted, so refresh behavior is unchanged.

[WebUI Toolbar] Fix FocusMenuBarByAltKey with WebUI Menu Button

In BrowserKeyEventsTest.FocusMenuBarByAltKey, pressing and releasing
the Alt key focuses the app menu via
ToolbarView::SetPaneFocusAndFocusAppMenu(). When the WebUI Menu Button
(kWebUIAppMenuButton) is enabled, WebUIAppMenuControl focuses
WebUIToolbarInternalWebView (View ID 0, not VIEW_ID_APP_MENU) and sends
an asynchronous OnFocusRequested(kAppMenu) Mojo IPC to
<app-menu-button>, which reports focus back via
onAppMenuFocusChanged(true) -> ToolbarView::GetAppMenuFocused().

Replace EXPECT_TRUE(IsViewFocused(VIEW_ID_APP_MENU)) with
base::test::RunUntil waiting on ToolbarView::GetAppMenuFocused().

policy: Allow INITIALIZATION_STATUS_ERROR in ActivityStorage

Commit 274d9b14433540 converted the PrefService initialization status
DCHECK in ActivityStorage::ActivityStorage to a non-fatal CHECK, which
triggered DumpWithoutCrashing reports in production when constructing
ActivityStorage with PrefService::INITIALIZATION_STATUS_ERROR and was
temporarily reverted back to DCHECK in https://crrev.com/c/8629867.

On ChromeOS, when a user's Preferences or Local State file on disk is
corrupt or unreadable (e.g. JSON parse error), JsonPrefStore initializes
an empty in-memory dictionary and completes initialization while
GetInitializationStatus() returns INITIALIZATION_STATUS_ERROR. Since
commit cd8c165ed4de2, callers construct ActivityStorage whenever the
status is not INITIALIZATION_STATUS_WAITING, and ActivityStorage
operates safely against the in-memory dictionary.

Replace the temporary DCHECK exclusion with a non-fatal CHECK_NE
asserting that the PrefService status is not
INITIALIZATION_STATUS_WAITING, and add a unit test covering
INITIALIZATION_STATUS_ERROR.

[remoting] Ignore FlagsChanged events in macOS keyboard input monitor

When switching active applications on macOS (e.g. via Cmd+Tab),
WindowServer synthesizes a modifier-synchronization kCGEventFlagsChanged
event with pid == 0 and kCGKeyboardEventKeycode == 0 (kVK_ANSI_A).
LocalKeyboardInputMonitorMac previously mapped keycode 0 to USB KeyA
(0x070004) and reported it as local keyboard input, blocking remote
input for 2 seconds and causing the auto-hidden disconnect bar to
reappear.

Stop subscribing the keyboard event tap to kCGEventFlagsChanged and only
treat kCGEventKeyDown and kCGEventKeyUp as local keyboard input in
GetLocalKeyboardEventUsbKeycode(). Legitimate local keyboard activity
triggers key-down and key-up events, whereas ignoring
kCGEventFlagsChanged avoids false positives from synthetic WindowServer
modifier-state notifications.

[viz] Move full screen video detection into full_screen_video_util

OverlayProcessorWin::TryPromoteFullScreenVideo and
DCLayerOverlayProcessor::IsPossibleFullScreenLetterboxing detect a full
screen, possibly letterboxed or pillarboxed, video. A follow-up CL needs
the same detection on Ozone/Wayland to decide when an HDR video's
metadata can be passed through to the system compositor.

This CL moves the detection into full_screen_video_util.{h,cc}:
  * ContainedAndCenteredRect(): previously an anonymous helper in
    overlay_processor_win.cc. It now returns an empty rect for an empty
    input instead of dividing by zero.
  * IsPossibleFullScreenLetterboxing(): previously a static method of
    DCLayerOverlayProcessor.
  * GetFullScreenVideoRect(): the fit-and-centered and clip checks from
    TryPromoteFullScreenVideo, with the tolerance as a parameter. The
    one pixel tolerance becomes kFullScreenVideoTightTolerance.

OverlayProcessorWin and DCLayerOverlayProcessor now use these helpers.
There is no behavior change on Windows. Adds
full_screen_video_util_unittest.cc.

Fix PrerenderHostRegistry critical memory pressure & re-enable test

In crrev.com/c/7833126, PrerenderHostRegistry was migrated to
base::MemoryConsumer. However, GetCurrentMemoryLimit() was
introduced to return default capacity (100) whenever
base::kStatefulMemoryPressure was disabled. As a result, critical
memory pressure events (memory_limit == 0) were ignored in
CreateAndStartHost, failing to reject new prerender triggers with
kMemoryPressureOnTrigger.

This CL resolves the issue by querying memory_limit() directly in
CreateAndStartHost to reject new prerenders when under critical
memory pressure (<= kCriticalMemoryPressureThreshold).

It also inlines the base::kStatefulMemoryPressure check into
GetScaledLimit() and removes GetCurrentMemoryLimit(), which was
conflating critical pressure checks with stateful limit scaling.

Finally, this CL re-enables the disabled browser test:
MultiplePrerendersBrowserTest.MemoryPressureOnTrigger_Critical.

Android: Abort test runs when devices go offline mid-shard

When an Android device or emulator goes offline mid-shard (`adb: device
offline`), `ClearAllTombstones` previously swallowed
`DeviceUnreachableError` in `_ListTombstones`, causing `_ArchiveLogcat`
(`adb logcat -c`) to hit a 90s `CommandTimeoutError` on every remaining
batch. `LocalDeviceTestRun._RunTestsOnDevice` treated
`CommandTimeoutError` as a normal test timeout (`ResultType.TIMEOUT`)
and reset `consecutive_device_errors`, wasting 90s per batch instead of
aborting the unreachable device and leaving remaining batches `NOTRUN`
for retry.

Additionally, skip `RetryOnSystemCrash` retries (`retries=0`) on
emulators instead of waiting 9 minutes (`3 * 180s`) for recovery:
QuickBoot AVDs do not self-recover when QEMU exits or hangs, and
`WaitUntilFullyBooted` restarts the shared host `adb` server. Across
16.0M `chromium.tests.avd` shards over 30 days, `Device is unreachable.
Waiting for recovery...` logged `Device never recovered. X(` on
1,113/1,114 (99.9%) attempts and 0/372 shards recovered to pass (vs.
28%-57% recovery on physical devices).

parent
cdf14f769c9210880e9f1bda38ebdd49cbab955d [ diff ] 
ios: Patch EarlGrey to track programmatic UIScrollView animations

In EarlGrey, UIScrollView+GREYApp only swizzles interactive drag and
deceleration methods (_scrollViewWillBeginDragging,
_scrollViewDidEndDraggingWithDeceleration:,
_stopScrollDecelerationNotify:) and relies on UIAnimation+GREYApp
(markStart:/markStop) to track programmatic
-[UIScrollView setContentOffset:animated:YES] animations.

Starting in iOS 27.1, UIKit drives programmatic UIScrollView scroll
animations via _takeScrollAnimatingAssertionWithReason:
(_scrollAnimatingViaAssertion) instead of keeping UIAnimation+GREYApp
busy across the animation. Consequently, EarlGrey considers the app
idle before the scroll animation completes and before
-scrollViewDidEndScrollingAnimation: fires, causing TabSwitcher
transition tests to tap moving GridCells mid-scroll or observe stale
page state.

Patch UIScrollView+GREYApp.m to swizzle -setContentOffset:animated:,
-_delegateScrollViewAnimationEnded, and
-_stopScrollingNotify:pin:tramplingAnimationDependentFlags: so
programmatic scroll animations are tracked under
kGREYPendingUIScrollViewScrolling while isScrollAnimating is YES.

With the new startup flow, a SearchInChromeIntent whose search phrase
only contains whitespace triggered a search for a blank query. The
legacy flow trims the phrase and opens the NTP with the omnibox focused
instead. Shortcuts donated by older Chrome versions still carry a single
space as search phrase, so align the new flow with the legacy behavior.

[PrivateAi] Queue transport errors during in-flight handshake

When a TLS handshake fails on the server, the server often sends a fatal
TLS alert frame immediately followed by a WebSocket close frame. Because
TlsSecureChannelImpl::OnIncomingFrameReceived previously handled
!frame.has_value() before checking handshake_frame_in_flight_, a
back-to-back handshake frame and WebSocket close would immediately tear
down oak_session_ while ProcessHandshakeFrame was still in flight to the
sandboxed OakSessionService utility process. This dropped the Mojo reply
before OnProcessHandshakeFrameDone could record the
PrivateAi.Tls.HandshakeStatus UMA histogram or trigger certificate cache
refresh on kCertVerificationFailed.

Queue incoming base::expected<std::vector<uint8_t>, TlsWebSocketClient::Error>
events in pending_incoming_frames_ whenever a handshake frame is in
flight so frames and transport close events are processed in arrival
order after OnProcessHandshakeFrameDone completes.

[Signin] Delete SyncConfirmationUI and handler

SyncConfirmationUI, SyncConfirmationHandler, and the
chrome://sync-confirmation WebUI resources previously drove the legacy
pre-UNO sync confirmation modal and window dialogs. With
TurnSyncOnHelper deleted, the loading spinner extracted into
HistorySyncOptinUI, and all test callers migrated to HistorySyncOptinUI,
SyncConfirmationUI and its WebUI resources are now unused.

Delete SyncConfirmationUI, SyncConfirmationHandler, their WebUI
resources and tests,
SigninViewController::ShowModalSyncConfirmationDialog(),
SigninViewControllerDelegate::CreateSyncConfirmationDelegate(),
LoginUIService::SyncConfirmationUIClosed(), and the SyncConfirmation
test helpers in login_ui_test_utils. Also remove the unused sync
confirmation strings, icons, user actions, and WebUI host/URL metrics
metadata.

This reverts commit ec5baad52086acbf4cd4b70d8b8d2205cbb1b0ad.

Reason for revert: Build failures

Original change's description:
> [Full WebUI Omnibox] Test real clicks to open popup and place caret.
>
> This CL adds the following new tests based on an audit of uncovered full
> WebUI Omnibox popup CUJs:
>
> - `ClickUnfocusedOmniboxOnHttpsPageOpensZeroSuggest` (both toolbars):
>   the popup is Full, focused, with no user input, the elided URL fully
>   selected, and the dropdown showing the results of a zero-prefix query.
>   Catches a click that stops opening the popup, querying zero-prefix
>   suggestions, focusing the WebUI input, or selecting all.
>
> - `SecondClickMidWordOnElidedUrlUnelidesAndPlacesCaret` (both toolbars):
>   navigates to `https://127.0.0.1:<port>/title1.html`, clicks the
>   omnibox to open the popup on the elided URL
>   (`127.0.0.1:<port>/title1.html`), waits past the 500 ms window during
>   which the newly opened popup forwards clicks to the browser window,
>   and clicks mid-word in the "/title1.html" path (between "ti" and
>   "tle1", found by measuring the text with the input's font). Verifies
>   that the input unelides to the full `https://...` URL with the caret
>   placed at that same character, shifted past "https://". Catches
>   uneliding on press (which would put the caret at the click position in
>   the shifted text), not uneliding, and keeping the select-all.
>
> - `ClickUnfocusedOmniboxOnNtpOpensZeroSuggest` and
>   `ClickUnfocusedOmniboxOnSrpOpensZeroSuggest` (Views toolbar only): as
>   above, on the NTP (empty input) and on a search results page. The new
>   `FullWebUIOmniboxFakeGoogleSrpInteractiveTest` fakes a Google SRP by
>   pointing `--google-base-url` at an HTTPS test server. The tests also
>   check the page classification, so they really cover the NTP and the
>   SRP.
>
> These last two tests don't run with the WebUI toolbar, where they are
> flaky (NTP 3/5, SRP 0/5 locally). There,
> `WebUIReadOnlyOmnibox::OnPointer()` makes the popup start two
> zero-prefix queries for one click (via `OpenOmniboxIfFullPopup(true)`
> and `SyncNativeStateToWebUI(kQueryZps)`). The second clears the popup's
> matches, and `SearchboxHandler::QueryAutocomplete()` drops it because
> the first is still running, so nothing is redrawn until that query sends
> another update, which in the test it never does. That race is tracked in
> b:578537342.
>

PrivateAi: Populate URLLoaderFactoryParams in TlsCertificateDownloader

TlsCertificateDownloader::GetURLLoaderFactory() previously passed a
default-constructed network::mojom::URLLoaderFactoryParams::New() to
NetworkContext::CreateURLLoaderFactory(). Because
URLLoaderFactoryParams::process_id (network::OriginatingProcessId) is a
non-nullable Mojo union that default-constructs to an empty union state,
serializing it over Mojo to the out-of-process Network Service fails
validation with VALIDATION_ERROR_DESERIALIZATION_FAILED and crashes the
Network Service process.

Additionally, browser-process SimpleURLLoader requests created without a
request_initiator must use RequestMode::kNoCors (and a trusted factory
with automatically_assign_isolation_info = true and is_orb_enabled =
false) so CorsURLLoaderFactory::IsValidRequest() does not reject the
request.

Printing: Disallow Print Preview for non-user BrowserContexts on CrOS

PrintPreviewDialogController::GetOrCreatePreviewDialog() checks
HasWebContentsModalDialogHost() before creating a Print Preview dialog
for a non-tab WebContents. However, on ChromeOS, several UIs that run in
non-user BrowserContexts (such as the Login, OOBE, and Lock screens) do
attach a WebContentsModalDialogHost.

Check ash::IsUserBrowserContext() in GetOrCreatePreviewDialog() on
ChromeOS so that Print Preview is rejected for non-user BrowserContexts.
Also add browser tests covering GetOrCreatePreviewDialog() for non-tab
WebContents without a modal dialog host and for non-user
BrowserContexts.

Use SIMD packing for short Latin-1 AtomicString signatures

Replace scalar byte-by-byte packing with the existing SIMD-capable
ConvertTo8BitHashReader when constructing small-string cache signatures
from UTF-16 input known to contain only Latin-1 characters. The current
byte-by-byte packing is SIMD vectorized on certain platforms (e.g. ARM)
but this isn't universal.

Reuse SSE2 and NEON implementations for four and eight-character
packing, retaining the scalar fallback.

This has overall improvements in the overall Speedometer3 score,
depending on the platform:

win-11-perf - 0.3%

android-pixel4-perf - 0.2%

android-pixel10-perf - 0.1%

[Safe Browsing] Populate initiator source on pending new-tab navs

When a link without target="_blank" is opened in a new tab via
Ctrl+click or middle-click, WebContentsImpl::OpenURL calls
OpenURLFromTab (Navigate()), which starts the navigation in the new tab
(DidStartNavigation) synchronously before firing DidOpenRequestedURL
(RecordNewWebContents). Because the pending NavigationEvent is created
with an empty source_url and an earlier last_updated timestamp than the
subsequent retargeting NavigationEvent from RecordNewWebContents,
IdentifyReferrerChainByPendingEventURL fails to link the pending new-tab
navigation back to the source tab.

To fix this, when DidStartNavigation creates a renderer-initiated
pending_nav_event with an empty source_url and an initiator
RenderFrameHost belonging to a different WebContents, populate
source_url, source_main_frame_url, and source_tab_id on
pending_nav_event directly from the initiator frame. Also update
TestSafeBrowsingNavigationObserverManager to observe newly created
WebContents upon creation so DidStartNavigation on new tabs created via
OpenURLFromTab is observed in browser tests, matching production
TabFeatures initialization.

Bug: b:568560137
Test: browser_tests --gtest_filter=SBNavigationObserverBrowserTest.IdentifyReferrerChainByPendingEventURL*

Queue PageContentCache::RemovePageContentForTab before store init

Previously, PageContentCache::RemovePageContentForTab posted directly
to PageContentStore on the background sequence even when
store_initialized_ was false, unlike CachePageContent and
GetPageContentForTab. This meant a tab removal requested before
OSCryptAsync finished initializing the store would run on the database
sequence ahead of earlier writes queued in pending_tasks_, leaving
deleted tab entries behind once OnStoreInitialized drained the queue.

This change queues RemovePageContentForTab in pending_tasks_ when
store_initialized_ is false so all store operations execute in FIFO
order.

Disable FuzzTest coverage instrumentation on Linux ASan LSan Builder

Sanitizer builds on Linux enable `enable_fuzztest_fuzz` by default so
that test binaries support FuzzTest's --fuzz mode. This instruments all
code with -fsanitize-coverage=inline-8bit-counters (~12M counters in
interactive_ui_tests), adding overhead to every basic block. CI never
runs tests with --fuzz; FUZZ_TESTs still run as regular gtests
(unit-test mode), which doesn't use coverage feedback.

data_protection: Skip drawing empty watermark in navigation controller

This CL updates `DataProtectionNavigationController::
ApplyDataProtectionSettingsOrDelayIfEmpty()` to clear the
`WatermarkTextContainer` via `SetWatermarkText(nullptr, 0, 0)` when
`settings.watermark_text` is empty and `kEnableSkipEmptyWatermark` is
enabled, instead of calling `DrawWatermarkToPaintRecord()` and
`ToSkPicture()` on an empty string. This avoids resolving the watermark
`gfx::FontList` and recording an empty `cc::PaintRecord` and `SkPicture`
on every unwatermarked navigation while still clearing any previously
set watermark for printing.

data_protection: Skip building and painting empty watermark in overlay

Every `ContentsContainerView` constructs a `DataProtectionOverlayView`
during `BrowserView` construction, which previously called
`UpdateWatermarkBlock("", ...)` unconditionally. Even for empty text,
`DrawWatermarkToPaintRecord()` resolves a platform `gfx::FontList` in
`GetWatermarkBlockWidth()`, and `DataProtectionOverlayView::OnPaint()`
calls `DrawWatermark()` to tile empty `drawPicture()` commands across
the viewport.

This CL default-initializes `width` and `height` to 0 in
`WatermarkBlock` and, when `kEnableSkipEmptyWatermark` is enabled,
skips the initial `UpdateWatermarkBlock("", ...)` call in the
`DataProtectionOverlayView` constructor, resets `watermark_block_ = {}`
when `text` is empty in `UpdateWatermarkBlock()`, and returns early in
`OnPaint()` when `watermark_block_.record.empty()`.

On Linux Release Crossbench `browser-startup` (N=32 repetitions per
story), this reduces end-to-end startup latency across stories:
- `Startup.BrowserWindow.FirstPaint` P50 (median):
  -3.50 ms (-2.6%, 95% CI [-4.50, -2.50] ms) on `blank_startup`,
  -2.50 ms (-1.9%, 95% CI [-4.00, -0.50] ms) on `newtab_startup`,
  -1.50 ms (-1.1%, 95% CI [-3.00, -0.50] ms) on `google_startup`
- `InitialWebUI.Startup.ReloadButton.FirstContentfulPaint`
  P50 (median): -3.50 ms (-1.6%) on `blank_startup`,
  -3.50 ms (-1.5%) on `newtab_startup`, -2.00 ms (-0.9%) on
  `google_startup`
- `Startup.FirstWebContents.NonEmptyPaint3` P50 (median):
  -3.50 ms (-1.6%, 95% CI [-5.00, -1.50] ms) on `blank_startup`,
  -2.50 ms (-0.9%) on `newtab_startup`, -2.00 ms (-0.8%) on
  `google_startup`

omnibox: Optionally create the AI Mode popup only on demand

With OmniboxAimPopupDeferCreation, the AI Mode popup no longer creates
its WebUI content while the browser window is built, but it still
creates it shortly after the window's first frame. Every window ends up
with an AI Mode WebContents and renderer document, so the deferral
moves the work off the first frame without lowering the steady-state
cost.

Add the create_on_first_presentation param to
OmniboxAimPopupDeferCreation, default true, which keeps the current
behavior. When it is false, the AI Mode presenter does not request the
post-presentation creation, and the content is created only by the
existing EnsureWebUIContentCreated() callers: showing the popup, the
classic popup's context menu and the location bar actions. Windows that
never open AI Mode never create it.

This gives a Finch arm that trades AI Mode first-show latency for
memory. On ChromeOS 4 GB devices (ui.LoginPerf.noarc_2windows, full
WebUI build, deferral on vs. this param off), the popup renderer's PSS
was 28 MiB lower on grunt and on awasuki, with no login regression.

SuperSize: Gzip on a background thread in SaveSizeInfo

Add _BackgroundWriter to buffer serialized .size output into 1 MiB
chunks and forward them via a bounded queue to a background thread
writing to GzipFile. Since zlib releases the GIL, gzip compression
overlaps with Python serialization while avoiding buffering the entire
uncompressed .size file in memory.

Expected speed-up: 7.3s -> 5.6s for file_format.SaveSizeInfo() on an
is_official_build=true x64 build of Chrome.minimal.apks (identical
output).

1. Replace the lazy (.*?) match in _REGEX with a greedy ([^|\n]*)

is_official_build=true x64 build of Chrome.minimal.apks (identical
output).

Overwrite gainmap pixels in SoftwareImageDecodeCacheUtils

In GenerateCacheEntryFromCandidate(), the scaled gainmap image is drawn
into newly allocated discardable memory using SkCanvas::drawImageRect().
Passing a null SkPaint defaults to SkBlendMode::kSrcOver, which can
leave uninitialized bytes in the destination buffer if the candidate
gainmap is non-opaque.

Use SkBlendMode::kSrc when drawing the scaled gainmap so the destination
buffer is always overwritten. Also mark the decoded gainmap SkImageInfo
as kOpaque_SkAlphaType in DoDecodeImage(). The gainmap should always be
opaque and it matches SkImageInfo created in
DeferredImageDecoder::CreateGainmapGenerator().

[Omnibox] Populate icon_path on current_match in SetInputState

When switching back to a tab with uncommitted edits in the Full WebUI
Omnibox, OmniboxPopupHandler::SetInputState synthesizes
state->current_match from controller_->edit_model()->CurrentMatch(), but
omitted mojom_match->icon_path. When favicon lookup fails for an
unvisited modified URL, SearchboxIconElement::computeMaskImage_()
returns url() and masks out the left-hand-side icon completely.

Expose `SearchboxHandler::VectorIconToResourceName`
and populate mojom_match->icon_path in `OmniboxPopupHandler::SetInputState`using `current_match.GetVectorIcon`.
Also guard SearchboxIconElement::computeMaskImage_() against empty
iconPath values.

Disable FuzzTest coverage instrumentation on Linux UBSan Builder

Sanitizer builds on Linux enable `enable_fuzztest_fuzz` by default so
that any test binary can be run with FuzzTest's --fuzz mode. This turns
on `use_sanitizer_coverage`, which instruments all code with
-fsanitize-coverage=inline-8bit-counters (interactive_ui_tests has ~18M
counters), adding overhead to every basic block.

CI never runs tests with --fuzz; FUZZ_TESTs still run as regular gtests
without it. Disable it on Linux UBSan Builder, where
interactive_ui_tests shards regularly hit the 60 minute timeout, to
reduce test runtime.

Disabling it also turns off `use_sanitizer_coverage`, which
//build/toolchain/concurrent_links.gni used to budget 24GB per link.
The 8GB default instead allows ~14 concurrent links on this bot, and
the large UBSan test binary links fill the disk. Pin
`concurrent_links` to 4 to keep the previous link concurrency.

[sda] Make ViewTimelineOptions and subject mandatory

CSSWG issue with resolution:
https://github.com/w3c/csswg-drafts/issues/13959

A ViewTimeline is not useful without a subject, since the subject
member is readonly. You essentially have a timeline that is forever
inactive.  The CSSWG resolved to make ViewTimelineOptions mandatory
in the constructor, and the subject mandatory within the options.

This path resolves the remaining interop failure for scroll-
animations.

Persist legal_message_token in EntityTable for Sync retries

When a new Wallet pass (`kServerWallet` `EntityInstance`) is added
locally, `ValuableSyncBridge::EntityInstanceChanged()` passes its
`legal_message_token` to `change_processor()->Put()`. However,
`ClientTagBasedDataTypeProcessor::Put()` only caches trimmed specifics
in Sync metadata (`TrimAllSupportedFieldsFromRemoteSpecifics()` clears
`legal_message_token`), and if the initial `Commit` RPC fails (or the
browser restarts before the commit completes), the subsequent Sync retry
fetches the entity payload via `ValuableSyncBridge::GetDataForCommit()`,
which previously reconstructed `EntityData` with an empty
`legal_message_token`.

This CL persists `legal_message_token` in the
`autofill_ai_entities_metadata_wallet` SQLite table (WebDatabase version
161) when a Wallet entity is locally created:
- `ValuableSyncBridge::GetDataForCommit()` attaches any stored
  `legal_message_token` for the pass keys being committed on retry.
- Local edits to an entity while its initial creation commit is still
  unsynced preserve the pending token in `EntityTable` and include it in
  `ValuableSyncBridge::EntityInstanceChanged()`.
- Once the commit succeeds (`!IsEntityUnsynced()`),
  `ValuableSyncBridge::ApplyIncrementalSyncChanges()` clears any
  non-empty `legal_message_token` (and incoming remote Sync writes clear
  it explicitly) so the single-use token is not resent on later updates.

7dd6b979ac631b73929ef3255ca0d1c8c77a6f95 [ diff ] 
Reland "[ash] camera_app: pass the MediaDeviceSaltService to CameraAppUI"

This is a reland of commit 460547cbecc338377d167486fb005d9b2cf3b9e4.

The difference from the original is that CameraAppUI takes the service
as a nullable pointer, TranslateVideoDeviceId() keeps its fallback to
the browser context's unique ID, and CameraAppIntegrationTest also runs
in a guest session.

The original crashed when the camera app was opened in a guest session.
It made the MediaDeviceSaltService a required constructor parameter, but
MediaDeviceSaltServiceProvider::Find() returns null for every guest
session: BrowserContextHelper::GetBrowserContextByUser() substitutes the
off-the-record context when the user is a guest, and
MediaDeviceSaltServiceFactory is kOriginalOnly, so it has no service for
an off-the-record profile. The fallback the original removed was
reachable after all.

Guest sessions therefore behave exactly as they did before. The
decoupling is unchanged:
CameraAppUIDelegate::GetMediaDeviceSaltService() is still gone and
chrome/browser/ash/system_web_apps/apps/camera_app still does not reach
MediaDeviceSaltServiceFactory. Incognito stays out of the test: the
camera app does not run there, and ChromeCameraAppUIDelegate CHECKs on a
missing CameraSaveHandler long before anything here is reached.

Original change's description:
> [ash] camera_app: pass the MediaDeviceSaltService to CameraAppUI
>
> CameraAppUI uses the MediaDeviceSaltService in one place, to build the
> camera app device provider, so it takes the service as a constructor
> parameter. MakeCameraAppUIConfig() resolves it through
> ash::MediaDeviceSaltServiceProvider, keyed on the profile's AccountId,
> the way MakeRecorderAppUIConfig() does next to it.
>
> CameraAppUIDelegate::GetMediaDeviceSaltService() is gone, so
> chrome/browser/ash/system_web_apps/apps/camera_app no longer reaches
> MediaDeviceSaltServiceFactory. The directory keeps its
> chrome/browser/media/webrtc allowance for the process-wide
> MediaCaptureDevicesDispatcher.
>

WebUILocationBar: Fix HidesWhenTypingInOmnibox toast test

When WebUILocationBar is enabled, BrowserView::SetFocusToLocationBar()
requests focus in the WebUI toolbar renderer asynchronously over Mojo
via ToolbarUIObserver::OnFocusRequested, while WebUIReadOnlyOmnibox
marks has_focus_ synchronously on the browser side.

In HidesWhenTypingInOmnibox, SendKeyPressSync() was called immediately
after SetFocusToLocationBar() before the WebUI toolbar processed the
focus request and focused its inner input element. Under TSAN, the key
event arrived before the input element had focus, causing
OmniboxInputWaiter::Wait() to time out. Similarly, in
SetUpOnMainThread() and RemoveOmniboxFocus(), waiting only on
WaitForViewFocus() did not settle the WebUI toolbar page focus or Mojo
pipes.

Introduce FocusOmnibox(), WaitForOmniboxFocus(), and
SettleWebUIToolbarFocus() helpers that wait for document.hasFocus() on
the WebUI toolbar page and flush the WebUI toolbar Mojo pipes so focus
changes settle before subsequent test actions run. In
ToastReactToOmniboxFocus, using FocusOmnibox() also allows replacing
an asynchronous base::test::RunUntil() check with a synchronous
EXPECT_FALSE() check on the toast widget's visibility.

[masonry] Update visibility to be computed before rule-break

In line with recent edits to the css-gaps spec, we are updating the
`rule-visibility` states for grid lanes to be computed pre `rule-break`
rather than post `rule-break`. The change that introduced
`rule-visibility` for `grid-lanes` was under the impression that the
spec would change to apply them post `rule-break`, however after
discussion that turned out to not be the case.

With this CL, we now compute the visibility state for every lane (gap)
by checking whether each segment in the gap has a "empty" window
adjacent to it.

The methods were moved to GapGeometry now since it makes more sense for
the utils to be there rather than in the painter.

The overall complexity class of the gap decorations painter does not
change.

Some edits were needed to two WPTs that tested the wrong behavior
assumed by the previous CL.

https://drafts.csswg.org/css-gaps-1/#visibility

Avoid dangling AtomicString refs across WillModifyAttribute

When Element::DidMoveToNewDocument moves an element between documents
with different quirks modes, GetIdAttribute() and GetClassAttribute()
return const AtomicString& references into the element's
AttributeVector backing buffer. If a DevTools attribute-modified DOM
breakpoint pauses execution inside WillModifyAttribute and script
mutates the element's attributes, AttributeVector can reallocate and
leave new_value dangling in SetAttributeInternal and
DidModifyAttribute.

Copy the attribute values in DidMoveToNewDocument and
SetAttributeInternal before calling WillModifyAttribute, and
re-validate the attribute index after WillModifyAttribute in the
modified-value branch.

glic: Block restricted copies and show paste-block modals

Pasting into Glic during an in-flight cloud copy scan or after a
restricted copy completes inserts replacement warning text into the
composer or fails silently without a paste-block modal. In addition,
staging Glic page-context eligibility before async copy checks finish
loses copy-time eligibility across copy warning dialogs, cloud copy
scans, and multi-format copies with trailing empty text.

Wrap copy policy callbacks at the ChromeContentBrowserClient boundary
(guest_util.{h,cc}) to bind copy-time Glic eligibility when allowed
clipboard writes complete, and gate pastes into Glic to silently reject
CopyRestrictionLevel::kOngoingScan copies while showing paste-block
modals on blocked copies and closed kKeptInManagedChrome source tabs.

CONV=804498f0-fc56-4f71-b6a4-78c3191fdf9c

This reverts commit 3cd6a93e1ea388fe104d65c3e4b8e21c3c5aecc7.

Reason for revert: 
The Suspect CL https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/q/Ie5b5b462f91529663585fc448633af561f606198 is highly likely the cause of the crash. Please see the crash report http://crash/8b72ff4708400000.
Rebase the Revert CL on top of main branch with conflicts allowed option to prevent false positive merge conflicts.

If you agree with the revert CL, please approve it and mark as Commit-Queue +2 to submit it.

More details can be found in the go/crash-revert-cls-creation.

Original change's description:
> [Mac] Re-enable BeginFrameArgsTest.InvalidUnthrottledInterval
> 
> Re-enables the `unthrottled_interval` `DCHECK_LE` in
> `BeginFrameArgs::BeginFrameArgs()` and the corresponding
> `BeginFrameArgsTest.InvalidUnthrottledInterval` death test on macOS.
> 
> When `unthrottled_interval` and its constructor `DCHECK_LE` were
> introduced in crrev.com/c/7429037, both the `DCHECK_LE` and the death
> test were temporarily disabled on macOS (`TODO(crbug.com/477242770)`)
> because `ExternalBeginFrameSourceMac` tracked `nominal_refresh_period_`
> and `min_refresh_interval_` separately and only updated
> `nominal_refresh_period_` in `OnDisplayLinkCallback()`, leaving
> `min_refresh_interval_` stale when the system display refresh rate
> increased. That underlying issue was resolved in crrev.com/c/7499754,
> which merged `nominal_refresh_period_` into `min_refresh_interval_` so
> `OnDisplayLinkCallback()` updates `min_refresh_interval_` on every
> VSync callback before applying subsampling.
> 
> Part of http://go/arthurmilchior-fix-all-test-skill-chrome for AI week.

[Mac] Fix and re-enable CancelMacNativePickerBeforeCapture

DesktopCaptureMacTest.CancelMacNativePickerBeforeCapture was disabled
on macOS in crrev.com/c/8257516 because it failed on macOS 13 bots
with callback_run evaluating to true after request.reset().

In CaptureScreenshotFromMacNativePicker(), the @available(macOS 14.0,
*) branch wrapped the completion callback with base::BindPostTask()
before posting to the UI thread, whereas the macOS < 14.0 fallback
invoked std::move(callback).Run(SkBitmap()) synchronously. Because
CreateScreenshotCaptureRequest() calls
CaptureScreenshotFromMacNativePicker() before returning the
MacScreenshotCaptureRequest handle, the completion callback ran
synchronously on macOS 13 before the caller could reset the request
handle to cancel the capture.

Wrap the callback with base::BindPostTask() before the macOS 14.0
availability check so the fallback also runs asynchronously on the
caller's sequence, and re-enable
DesktopCaptureMacTest.CancelMacNativePickerBeforeCapture.

Part of http://go/arthurmilchior-fix-all-test-skill-chrome for AI week.

[DeepCAF] Add directory loading to CustomFormControlScriptIndex

Add CustomFormControlScriptIndex::InitializeFromDirectory(), which reads
index.json and the script files it references from a directory on a
background sequence and passes the entries to SetEntries(). Nothing
calls it yet; a follow-up CL calls it at startup with a local directory
given on the command line.

index.json is a JSON list of {"host", "url_filter", "script_name"}
objects. If it can't be read or isn't a JSON list, the current entries
are kept. Items with missing or non-string fields, or with a
script_name that isn't a plain ASCII file name, are skipped, as are
scripts that can't be read or exceed
kMaxCustomFormControlScriptSizeBytes.

[WebUIToolbar] Fix CastBrowserControllerTest pixel tests

When a pinned or ephemeral toolbar action (<pinned-toolbar-action>) is
added to the WebUI toolbar, OverflowableToolbarActionContainerMixin
schedules a responsive layout pass on the next animation frame
('schedule-layout-responsive-controls') to shrink #location-bar, while
ToolbarActionMixin.registerHelpBubble_() synchronously registers the
element with TrackedElementManager in the Lit updated() cycle. As a
result, TrackedElementManager.startTracking() sends pre-layout bounds to
C++ (at the coordinates where #avatar moves on the next frame) and only
updates them after its 50ms debounce timer, causing immediate pixel
screenshots in CastBrowserControllerTest to capture the #avatar button.

Additionally, subsequent icon state changes (such as Idle -> Warning or
Idle -> Paused) coalesce state pushes via PostPushToolbarState() while
the TrackedElementWebUI is already registered, and
TestBrowserUi::VerifyPixelUi only waited on the Browser UI compositor
rather than the WebUI WebContents renderer compositor.

To fix this:
1. Dispatch 'layout-now' in ToolbarActionMixin.registerHelpBubble_()
   before calling registerHelpBubble() so responsive toolbar controls
   are laid out before TrackedElementManager reads
   getBoundingClientRect().
2. Flush WebUI toolbar pipes in
   CastBrowserControllerTest::VerifyCastButtonScreenshot when
   WebUIPinnedToolbarActions is enabled.
3. Wait for a copyable view in the WebContents in
   TestBrowserUi::VerifyPixelUi when verifying a TrackedElementWebUI
   with pixel verification enabled.

[MediaRecorder] Reset state on failed start and clear tracks

When MediaRecorderHandler::Start() fails, MediaRecorder::start() left
state_ as State::kRecording before throwing NotSupportedError. Because
HasPendingActivity() returns true whenever state_ != State::kInactive,
Oilpan retained the MediaRecorder for the life of the ExecutionContext.
Reset state_ to State::kInactive when Start() returns false, matching
step 14.3.1 of the MediaStream Recording spec.

In MediaRecorderHandler::Start(), defer registering the MediaStream
observer and setting timeslice_ until track and MIME type validation
succeeds, and call Stop() on early return paths. In
MediaRecorderHandler::Stop(), clear video_tracks_ and audio_tracks_ so
stopped recorders do not retain MediaStreamComponent instances that were
later removed from the MediaStream.

🌺 Revert "[Android] Hop on Public Transit in NewTabPageTestUtils"

This reverts commit ceea0dc765ebff65d0f57a3d4094c2e116d7ce11.

Reason for revert:
ToolbarTest#testIncognitoNtpAccessibilityOrder_OnEnterAndExitTabSwitcher (in chrome_public_test_apk) is consistently failing across 3 CI builds on 2 builders (#40770 and #40771 on chrome/ci/android-arm-tests, #5442 on chrome/ci/android-14-arm64-rel-tests, plus 2 flaky builds on chromium/ci/android-16-x64-rel and 14 distinct CQ try CLs), starting at:
https://ci.chromium.org/ui/p/chrome/builders/ci/android-arm-tests/40770
https://ci.chromium.org/ui/p/chrome/builders/ci/android-arm-tests/40771
https://ci.chromium.org/ui/p/chrome/builders/ci/android-14-arm64-rel-tests/5442

Changing NewTabPageTestUtils.waitForNtpLoaded(Tab) to hop onto IncognitoNewTabPageStation causes the test to time out waiting for @id/control_container to be effectively VISIBLE after exiting LayoutType.HUB with ControlsPosition.BOTTOM.

Please feel free to re-land once IncognitoNewTabPageStation / NewTabPageTestUtils.waitForNtpLoaded(Tab) handles bottom controls visibility after exiting the Hub tab switcher.

Original change's description:
> [Android] Hop on Public Transit in NewTabPageTestUtils
>
> NewTabPageTestUtils#waitForNtpLoaded() now hops on Public Transit at
> RegularNewTabPageStation / IncognitoNewTabPageStation and returns the
> Station, so tests that wait for the NTP end up holding a Station they
> can continue from as they are migrated. Existing callers don't need to
> change.
>
> NewTabPageTestUtils moves to chrome_java_transit, where the Stations
> are.
>
> Caveats:
> - Test infra that can't hop on, such as Public Transit entry points
>   starting on the NTP, keeps the previous wait, moved to
>   ChromeTabUtils#waitForNtpLoaded() and deprecated.
> - Tests that wait for an NTP the Stations don't model yet (no search
>   logo, focused Omnibox, the native NTP with the WebUI NTP override on
>   Android Desktop, and a garbage collection check) use the deprecated
>   wait, with TODOs.
> - Tests that already held the NTP Station from startOnNtp() no longer
>   call waitForNtpLoaded().
>

[Cast] Fix the bucket range of Cast Streaming bitrate histograms

CastStreaming.Sender.Video.Bitrate and
CastStreaming.Sender.{Audio,Video}.TransmissionRate record kbps with
UmaHistogramMemoryKB, which has a minimum of 1000. Every sample under
1 Mbps lands in the underflow bucket. That includes almost all audio
samples, since the default audio bitrate is 128 kbps, and any video
session that adapts below 1 Mbps.

Record these values with UmaHistogramCounts100000 instead, which
covers 1 kbps to 100 Mbps. Changing the bucket range changes the
meaning of the data, so the histograms get new names with a "2"
suffix, and the old names are removed.

OBSOLETE_HISTOGRAMS=Replaced by versions with a "2" suffix that use a kbps range.

This CL removes the unused `show_back_button` parameter and back button
callback plumbing from `QRCodeGeneratorBubbleController` and
`QRCodeGeneratorBubble`, since the desktop Sharing Hub is no longer

callers and is deleted.

[iOS] Add experimental setting to reset Magic Stack Tips state

Testing the natural Magic Stack Tips V2 priority train (impression caps,
interaction suppression, and eligibility signals) currently requires
deleting and reinstalling the app once a tip has been interacted with or
exhausted its 3-impression limit.
This CL adds a "Reset Magic Stack Tips State" toggle in Experimental
Settings so testers can reset all Magic Stack Tips impression counters,
interaction flags, signal history, and notification permissions on
startup without reinstalling Chrome or losing their current NTP
background configuration. Once triggered on launch, the toggle
automatically resets itself back to off so subsequent app launches
behave normally for multi-launch impression testing.

[Linux] Enable the GlobalShortcuts portal on GNOME

The GlobalShortcuts portal was disabled on GNOME because
xdg-desktop-portal-gnome returns an empty list from ListShortcuts, which
caused the shortcut dialog to be shown on every browser start. Since
the listener now binds a complete, persisted set of shortcuts that
GNOME accepts without a dialog, the workaround is no longer needed.

Enable the portal on GNOME and set preferred triggers by default, as on
other desktops. kGlobalShortcutsPortalPreferredTrigger can still
override the latter.

[DTC][Android] Read device signals consent from SigninPrefs

On Android, the enterprise signals disclaimer stores the user's consent
per account in SigninPrefs, keyed by the primary account's Gaia ID. The
profile-level kDeviceSignalsConsentReceived and
kDeviceSignalsPermanentConsentReceived prefs are never written on
Android, so UserPermissionServiceImpl::HasUserConsented() always
returned false there.

This CL makes HasUserConsented() read
SigninPrefs::GetDeviceSignalsPermanentConsentReceived() for the primary
account on Android. To support this, UserDelegate gets an Android-only
GetPrimaryAccountGaiaId(), implemented in UserDelegateImpl and
MockUserDelegate. It returns an empty GaiaId when there is no primary
account or no IdentityManager. In that case consent is treated as
missing, which also avoids the SigninPrefs CHECK on an empty Gaia ID.
That matters because the DTC navigation throttle calls
ShouldCollectConsent() on every navigation, including for signed-out
users.

The two profile prefs are no longer registered on Android, and
kDeviceSignalsConsentReceived is compiled out there. No pref deprecation
is needed because nothing on Android ever wrote them.
kDeviceSignalsPermanentConsentReceived stays defined on Android because
its string is reused as the SigninPrefs key.

This affects the DTC consumers of HasUserConsented():
ShouldCollectConsent(), CanCollectSignals() and
chrome://connectors-internals. Signal Sharing is unchanged. It will be
handled in a separate CL.

The temporary IsCollectSignalsConsentRequired() bypass for managed
profiles on Android is intentionally kept. It will be removed in a
follow-up CL once the disclaimer is rolled out.

Desktop, iOS and ChromeOS behavior is unchanged.

[gap-decorations] Fix flex rule with space-between

Flex gap decorations place each column rule at the midpoint of the
effective gap, which is the `gap` plus the space that `justify-content`
inserts between items.

For `space-around` and `space-evenly`, these values are equal, so the
rule was correct. However, I found a bug for `space-between` where with
exactly two items in a line, there is no space after the last item, so
the effective gap was only the `gap` value. As a result, the rule was
painted next to the second item instead of at the center of the gap.

This CL records the effective gap size from the space after the first
item, which is the space between the first two items.

This CL adds flex-gap-decorations-070 to cover the three distribution
values.

Cache Windows memory pressure commit histograms

Windows memory pressure sampling records three commit metrics on the
browser UI thread. The function-based UMA calls look up each histogram
on every sample, which can block on the StatisticsRecorder global lock.

The three calls now use cached UMA macros, avoiding repeated lookups
after initialization. Metric names, buckets and sampling behavior are
unchanged. The added test checks repeated samples.

Bug: 578297813
Test: Windows x64 Release memory-pressure tests (43 tests, 20 repeats)

[Linux] Forget GlobalShortcuts portal shortcuts of uninstalled extensions

GlobalAcceleratorListenerLinux persists the global shortcuts it has
offered to the portal, and binds them even when their owner isn't
loaded. Shortcuts of uninstalled extensions, and of extensions whose
commands were all removed by an update, were never removed.

Add GlobalAcceleratorListener::OnAcceleratorGroupRemoved(), and call it
from ExtensionCommandsGlobalRegistry when an extension is uninstalled or
loaded without commands, so that its shortcuts are no longer bound and
are dropped from the portal with the next bind. The session is closed
if nothing is left to bind. Shortcuts of disabled extensions are kept so
that re-enabling them doesn't show the dialog again.

Portals like KDE keep listing stored shortcuts until a bind without
them succeeds, so removed shortcuts are remembered as removed until
then, or until ListShortcuts stops reporting them. Otherwise they would
be passed through as untracked shortcuts and bound again.
